questions.stem: A client presents in an emotional crisis but has no immediate medical instability. What should the nurse prioritize early in crisis intervention?

questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Reserve seat-belt use mainly for highway travel because short local trips have minimal serious-injury risk.","B":"Adults seated in the rear seat can omit seat belts when the vehicle has front and side airbags.","C":"Wear a seat belt on every trip because consistent restraint use substantially reduces the risk of serious crash-related injury or death.","D":"Seat belts are primarily a pediatric intervention and add little protection after a passenger reaches adulthood."}}
questions.rationale: CDC states that seat belts are the most effective way to prevent injury or death in crashes for adults and older children and that they reduce serious crash-related injuries and deaths by about half. Consistent use on every trip is recommended.
questions.source_name: CDC — Facts About Seat Belt Use
questions.source_detail: Seat belts reduce serious crash-related injuries and deaths and should be used on every trip. CDC page dated 2026-01-27; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. questions.stem: A parent asks how to protect a 4-month-old infant from ultraviolet exposure. Which teaching is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use sunscreen as the primary protection for the infant because shade and clothing provide insufficient ultraviolet protection.","B":"Provide brief direct midday sun exposure each day because infants younger than 6 months are less susceptible to sunburn.","C":"Apply an adult sunscreen routinely to all exposed skin before using shade or protective clothing.","D":"Keep the 4-month-old out of direct sunlight when possible, use shade and protective clothing, and ask the pediatrician before applying sunscreen."}}
questions.rationale: FDA guidance recommends keeping infants younger than 6 months out of direct sunlight, using shade and protective clothing, and consulting a pediatrician before applying sunscreen to this age group. Sunscreen is not generally recommended as the primary protection for young infants.
questions.source_name: FDA — Should You Put Sunscreen on Infants? Not Usually
questions.source_detail: For infants younger than 6 months, FDA recommends shade and protective clothing and advises consulting a pediatrician before sunscreen use. questions.stem: What is the purpose of Mental Health First Aid training for community members?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Teach community members to recognize mental-health or substance-use challenges, provide initial support, and help connect the person with appropriate care.","B":"Teach community members to diagnose psychiatric disorders and select definitive treatment plans independently.","C":"Train nonclinicians to replace professional services by providing ongoing psychotherapy and medication management.","D":"Teach participants to avoid responding until a licensed clinician is physically present."}}
questions.rationale: Mental Health First Aid teaches participants to recognize signs of mental health or substance-use challenges, provide initial support, and help connect people with appropriate professional care. The program explicitly does not train participants to diagnose or replace professional treatment.
questions.source_name: Mental Health First Aid USA — Frequently Asked Questions
questions.source_detail: MHFA teaches recognition, response, first-level support, and connection to appropriate care; First Aiders do not diagnose or replace professional help. questions.stem: A client with PTSD begins experiencing a flashback during an assessment. Which nursing response is most appropriate initially?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Ask for a detailed narrative of the traumatic event while the flashback is occurring so the memory can be processed immediately.","B":"Speak calmly and use simple grounding cues that orient the client to the present situation and current surroundings.","C":"Leave the client alone until the episode ends because interaction generally prolongs trauma-related flashbacks.","D":"Challenge the accuracy of the traumatic memory during the flashback to help the client distinguish it from current reality."}}
questions.rationale: The VA National Center for PTSD describes grounding as a strategy for intrusive thoughts and flashbacks that helps the person focus on the current situation rather than the traumatic event. Calm, simple present-focused orientation is appropriate; detailed trauma processing is not the immediate goal during an acute flashback.
questions.source_name: VA National Center for PTSD — Grounding Technique
questions.source_detail: Grounding for intrusive thoughts/flashbacks: focus attention on the current situation and present sensory surroundings. Live VA National Center for PTSD page currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. questions.stem: A hospitalized client with heavy alcohol use develops severe tremor, confusion, hallucinations, and marked autonomic hyperactivity after stopping alcohol. Which condition should the nurse suspect?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Hepatic encephalopathy, which is established by tremor and hallucinations after abrupt alcohol cessation without further evaluation.","B":"Wernicke encephalopathy, which is defined by marked autonomic hyperactivity and hallucinations after stopping alcohol.","C":"Alcohol withdrawal delirium, a severe withdrawal syndrome requiring prompt medical treatment and close monitoring.","D":"A primary psychotic disorder, which is more likely than withdrawal when severe tremor and autonomic hyperactivity follow alcohol cessation."}}
questions.rationale: Alcohol withdrawal delirium is a severe withdrawal syndrome characterized by delirium with autonomic hyperactivity and can include hallucinations and marked tremor. It is medically dangerous and requires prompt treatment and monitoring rather than reassurance alone.
questions.source_name: American Society of Addiction Medicine — Alcohol Withdrawal Management Guideline
questions.source_detail: Alcohol withdrawal delirium: severe withdrawal with delirium/autonomic activation; recommendations VI.7–VI.13 address close monitoring and active medical management. ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline 2020 remains the active ASAM alcohol-withdrawal guideline; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
